value: mean preferred temperature (Tp) 23.44 C (SE 0.61, range 20.7 to 26.9 C) in a thermal gradient in spring, rising between late afternoon and early evening
units: categorical (mean selected body temperature, C, in a laboratory thermal gradient)

source.title: Preferred temperatures of Tarentola mauritanica in spring

method: thermal-gradient choice: ten adult specimens exposed to a thermal gradient, Tp measured at seven time intervals between 16 and 24 h
conditions: Population from NE Iberia, spring; 10 adults; Tp measured at seven time intervals between 16 and 24 h. Only the abstract was read (the article page and the abstract text returned by the page reader); the abstract does not say whether the geckos were taken from the wild for the trial, how long they were held, the gradient range or the date, so these are UNKNOWN to this record. The abstract also reports that mean, maximum and minimum Tp were inversely correlated with body size (SVL) and that this remained after size correction, and that spring Tp was much lower than in a previous summer study although diel variation persisted. No control group. Value is a mean across the ten animals and seven intervals as printed (mean +/- SE, range), a behavioural choice and not a receptor threshold.
quote: Tp values were low (23.44 ± 0.61 ºC, 20.7-26.9 ºC, mean ± SE, range) but geckoes gradually increased Tps between late afternoon and early evening.
note: Whole abstract sentence; the page reader returned it in two adjacent pieces ('Tp values were low (...)' and 'but geckoes gradually increased Tps between late afternoon and early evening.') that were joined.
